`null_resource.update_github_app_webhook` declares an explicit `depends_on` on `data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.data_cicd_secrets`, but the same data source is already referenced implicitly in `triggers.secret_version` (`data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.data_cicd_secrets[...].id`), so the explicit dependency is redundant.

`data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` has an explicit `depends_on` on `module.ec2_runners:module.runners`, but it already depends on that module implicitly via `for_each` over `module.runners.runners_map` (the parameter names are derived from the module's outputs).

`data.aws_ami.runner_ami` has an explicit `depends_on` on `module.ec2_runners:module.runners`, but it already depends on that module implicitly via `for_each` over `module.runners.runners_map` and via `data.aws_ssm_parameter.ami_id` (which itself reads from the module).

`module.github_app_runner_group` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), where `var.secrets_prefix` is built only from `var.tenant`/`var.deployment_config`. No attribute reference or depends_on ties the module to the secrets created and seeded by this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`), so on a fresh apply the data reads execute before the secrets and their seed versions exist and the plan fails. The root module's own `data_cicd_secrets` data sources carry exactly this depends_on, but this module does not.

`module.github_actions_job_logs` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), with no dependency on the secrets created and seeded in this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`). On a fresh apply the by-name data lookups run before the secrets exist, causing a plan failure; the lambdas' IAM policy documents also reference these data versions, so the whole module needs to be ordered after seeding.

`module.github_global_lock` reads its secrets via `data "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "secrets"` looked up by name (`${var.secrets_prefix}...`), with no dependency on the secrets created and seeded in this configuration (`aws_secretsmanager_secret.cicd_secrets` / `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets`). On a fresh apply the by-name data lookups run before the secrets exist, causing a plan failure; the clean-global-lock lambda's IAM policy also references these data versions.

`helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set` consumes a storage class purely by name: the value passed as `volume_requests_storage_type` is `"${namespace}-${type}-${sha1(tags)}"`, which exactly matches the `metadata.name` of the `kubernetes_manifest.storage_class` created in the parent `arc` module. There is no attribute reference or depends_on linking the release to that manifest, so on first apply the Helm release (and its PVC-consuming runner pods) can be created before the StorageClass exists, leaving PVCs unscheduled.

`helm_release.gha_runner_scale_set` references the service account only by name (`service_account` value), and the Kubernetes service account it names is created by `kubernetes_service_account_v1.runner_sa` (which also backs the `aws_eks_pod_identity_association.eks_pod_identity`). No dependency ties the Helm release to that SA resource, so the scale set's listener/runner pods can be deployed before the service account (and thus its pod-identity credentials) exists, breaking pod identity credential injection on startup.

`data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.data_cicd_secrets` declares an explicit `depends_on` on `data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.data_cicd_secrets`, but that dependency is already implied by its `secret_id = data.aws_secretsmanager_secret.data_cicd_secrets[each.key].id` reference. (The other entry in the depends_on — `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.cicd_secrets` — is legitimate and should be kept.)
